text:
**A.** Most states have abolished the fee tail and convert "to cousin and the heirs of his body" into a fee simple. That leaves the grantor with nothing to convey, so the niece takes nothing. The team note is accurate only for the minority of states that convert the grant to a life estate in the cousin with a remainder to his heirs. It doesn't describe most states, so I'm not changing my answer.

CONFIDENCE: 78
